name: Amaranthus

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Find alternate petiolate leaves and dense clusters of tiny, bracteate, usually greenish flowers. Then inspect leaf nodes for spines, stem hairs, sex distribution, bracts, tepals and mature fruit.
shared_traits: Annual herbs in the six-species learner set, with alternate simple leaves.
Minute flowers in axillary clusters and/or terminal spikes or panicles.
Reproductive structures include bracts, tepals and small one-seeded fruits.
shared_genus_recognition.caution: Do not use green flower color or pigweed habit alone; several species overlap strongly without mature flowers or fruits.

species_comparison_matrix.scleropoides: axillary clusters from base to top
species_comparison_matrix.spinosus: terminal staminate spikes, axillary pistillate clusters

species_comparison_matrix.palmeri: dioecious; male and female plants separate
species_comparison_matrix.spinosus: staminate upper and pistillate axillary clusters

species_comparison_matrix.palmeri: female bracts 4–6 mm, longer than tepals
species_comparison_matrix.polygonoides: five tepals partly joined at base
species_comparison_matrix.scleropoides: hardened swollen cluster axes; keeled pistillate bracts
species_comparison_matrix.spinosus: paired nodal spines remain best cue

species_key: Paired sharp spines at leaf nodes → A. spinosus.
No spines; low plant with hard swollen axillary cluster axes → A. scleropoides.
No spines; low plant with small congested axillary clusters, without hardened axes → examine A. polygonoides.
Tall plant with conspicuous hairy upper stem and thick inflorescence → A. retroflexus.
Tall nearly glabrous plant; male and female flowers on separate plants; long terminal spikes → A. palmeri.
Glabrous plant with slender interrupted terminal spikes; three tepals and wrinkled indehiscent fruit → A. viridis.
overlap_and_cautions: Young vegetative plants can be impossible to separate confidently.
Terminal spike size changes with maturity and site conditions.
A. palmeri must be checked for dioecy using flowering plants, not assumed from stature.
Bract, tepal and fruit traits require hand-lens or macro photography.
Do not confuse bracts with tepals when counting flower parts.

local_lookalike_routing.group: Other Amaranthus in the source pool
local_lookalike_routing.separate: Check mature female bracts, tepal number, fruit opening and node armature before species assignment.
Look at mealy leaf surfaces, leaf shape, and small flower clusters; use reproductive structure to confirm genus.
Acalypha has distinctive euphorb inflorescences and pistillate bracts, unlike Amaranthus flower clusters.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.role: fruit and tepal macro with scale

targeted_handoffs.request: Verify tepal counts and mature female-bract/utricle key for A. polygonoides versus A. scleropoides before declaring a deterministic pairwise key.
Use canonical species image records to find paired macros of nodes, female bracts, tepals and mature fruits; do not substitute whole-plant glamour shots.
